messages:
maria: Quick perf sweep idea — compare Ampere vs Hopper across regions for 7B models. Goal: prefill+decode p50/p95, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens. Models: Llama2-7b, Mistral-7b, Falcon-7b. Quants: fp16, int8, q4f16. Regions: us-west1 / us-east4 / eu-west1. Can infra spin up bench jobs? cc @kai @sophia :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sophia: I can run the micro-bench harness. What seq lengths? 512 for prefill and 2048 for decode mixed? :thinking:

james: yes — 512 prefill, 2048 mixed-decoder. Use batch sizes 1/4/8 to get latency vs throughput curve. Also capture kv-cache hit scenarios.

kai: I can provision nodes in all three regions but heads up: Hopper quota is tight in eu-west1, might need to fallback to us-east4 for some runs. I'll prioritize one Hopper per region and spin A100 pool.

james: running an initial job now for llama2-7b on Hopper(fp16) seq512 batch8:
```
rbench run --model llama2-7b --gpu hopper --quant fp16 --seq 512 --batch 8 --out s3://redwood-bench/1812346789/llama2-hopper-fp16-512.csv
```

deploy-bot: Job 98765 started by james — runner=bench-03, cfg=rbench-v2.3

deploy-bot: Job 98765 finished — p50_prefill_ms=42, p95_prefill_ms=110, decode_tokens_sec=5200, total_tokens=1_000_000

chris: cost calc quick note — spot prices used: ampere (a100) $2.40/hr, hopper (h100) $5.50/hr in us-west. Rough $/1M tokens = (gpu_time_hours * price)/1M_tokens. Using james' run -> ~ $18/1M on hopper(fp16) (very rough).

sophia: interesting — on small seq (512) p50 is similar, but for 2048 we expect Hopper to scale better due to tensor cores + larger memory bandwidth. Need kernel sweep: flash-attn v2 vs cutlass-based kernels vs tensor-expr.

maria: good. Can we add int8/q4f16 runs? Int8 tends to close cost gap. Also add a deterministic eval (perplexity/regression) for q4f16 on a short eval set so we don't miss quality regressions. @james can you add eval step post-run? :eyes:

james: will do. I'll run int8/q4f16 for each model after the fp16 baseline. Command example for q4f16:
```
rbench run --model mistral-7b --gpu ampere --quant q4f16 --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kernels flash_attn,cutlass --out s3://redwood-bench/1812346789/mistral-amp-q4-2048.csv
```

kai: scheduled kernel sweep jobs next Tue/Wed in non-prod. Also enabling fallback routing so if eu-west can't get H100 we'll run Hopper in us-east and tag the result with region_fallback=true.

deploy-bot: Job 98792 started for mistral-7b q4f16 (ampere)

deploy-bot: Job 98792 finished — p50_prefill_ms=58, p95_prefill_ms=145, decode_tokens_sec=3100

chris: preliminary cost summary from today's samples (spot-based, including prefill+decode):
- Hopper (fp16): ~ $17-20 / 1M tokens (high variance across regions)
- Ampere (fp16): ~ $11-13 / 1M tokens
- Ampere (q4f16): ~ $6-8 / 1M tokens (but need quality check)
These are rough; I'll formalize once we have full sweep.

sophia: quality note: q4f16 on Mistral had +0.6 perplexity on our chat-eval set vs fp16. Not huge but visible. We'll run full eval suite across models.

maria: summary so far: Hopper gives ~1.4-1.8x decode throughput on longer sequences and better p95 tail in many runs; Ampere still wins on cost for fp16, but quantization (q4f16/int8) flips economics a lot. Kernel choice affects p50 for decode (flash_attn tends to be best for these models). Next actions: 1) finish full region sweep for all models/quant combos, 2) kernel sweep, 3) produce final CSVs + notebook with plots (latency curves, tokens/sec, $/1M). Kai please flag any region fallbacks in results.

kai: ack — I'll annotate fallback runs and attach instance SKU/pricing metadata. Scheduling kernel sweep now.

maria: perfect — thanks team. Let's sync in next eng-ml stand if we have full results. :thumbsup:
